subject: Post-demo: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (EU/APAC data residency) - follow-up
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.inference

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.inference, marissa.cole@redwood.inference
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (EU/APAC data residency) - follow-up

Hi Anna \u0014

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning and walking us through FinBank's residency and compliance constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary requirement: all production customer data and inference requests must remain in the EU and must not be routed through non-EU regions for processing or caching.
- Secondary: KMS integration for tenant keys, SOC 2 / audit evidence required by procurement, and a desire for predictable SLOs and SLA-backed latency targets.
- Volume estimates you shared: ~400k LLM tokens/day initially with spikes during batch processing windows.

Deployment options discussed:
1) Hosted API (region-pin): fastest to ship, can pin requests to EU-only serving; however, cross-region failover may route to nearby regions in rare outage scenarios unless we explicitly disable cross-region fallback.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): single-tenant GPU pools in EU regions; better for throughput predictability and isolation; still managed by Redwood control plane but we can quarantine capacity to region.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): for strict residency and network isolation \u0014 customer-managed VPC, optional on-prem bundle; preferred when policy forbids any cross-border routing or third-party control plane access.

Attachments: I attached our region availability matrix and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) so your procurement team can see timelines and expected deliverables.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm whether cross-region fallback (for HA) is acceptable or must be disabled.
- If fallback must be disabled, we should prioritize Private or Dedicated with strict routing policies.
- Schedule a short technical call this week with Aditya (CC'd) to validate KMS and network requirements.

Availability: I can do Tue/Thu mornings CET; Aditya will share 30/45-min slots.

Thanks \u0014

Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments:
- redwood-region-availability.pdf (summary of EU/APAC region coverage and lead times)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP with milestones and owner rows)

Hi Lauren \u0014

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency requirement: must be EU-only for both data at-rest and in-transit processing. We cannot accept any processing or caching that leaves the EU boundary.
- Failover: cross-border failover is not acceptable for production traffic. If Redwood's hosted offering relies on cross-region routing to non-EU zones for failover, that will be a blocker.
- Compliance: procurement will need SOC 2 Type II and evidence of KMS/HSM integration options. We also need to understand encryption key custody options.
- Timeline: procurement is aiming for a Q3 contract if lead times and security posture align.

Can you confirm whether Hosted API can be configured to strictly prevent cross-region fallback? If not, please confirm timelines and costs for Dedicated (EU-only) vs Private VPC deployment. Also please include any lead time for KMS/HSM integration and what evidence (attestation) we can provide to auditors.

Best,
Anna
Anna Schmidt
Head of Cloud Security 
FinBank GmbH

Anna \u0014

Thanks \u0014 quick answers inline and next steps: 

1) Hosted API region pinning: we do offer EU-only region pinning for production traffic. By default we keep cross-region failover enabled for HA, but we can disable cross-region fallback at the tenant level if required. Disabling fallback will increase blast radius during regional outages; we'll document recovery tradeoffs in the MAP.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): single-tenant pools in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Lead time: typically 6-8 weeks from signed SOW for reserved capacity provisioning.

3) Private VPC/on-prem: delivery timeline dependent on whether you choose customer-hosted control plane or Redwood-managed private control plane; estimate 8-12 weeks depending on procurement of HSM and network approvals.

4) KMS/HSM: we support customer KMS with BYOK and HSM integrations (support for common providers: AWS KMS with CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, etc). We can provide KMS integration docs and implementation checklist for auditors.

Attached: SLA-draft-Redwood-vFinBank.docx (SLA + region lock appendix).

Next step: Aditya (CC) can run a short technical session to map KMS requirements and network architecture. If you confirm that cross-region fallback must be disabled, we should evaluate Dedicated vs Private (we can model costs in the MAP).

Proposed times for tech session: Mon Jun 21 10:00 CET / Tue Jun 22 09:00 CET / Wed Jun 23 14:00 CET. Please advise what works for you + procurement.

Thanks \u0014

Lauren

Anna / Lauren \u0014 quick technical note from infra: 

- Hosted: our EU-hosted endpoints can be tenant-pinned to EU regions and cross-region fallback can be disabled. When fallback is disabled, we do not replicate KV-caches or logs outside the pinned region; however, some control plane telemetry (non-customer-data operational metrics) may still flow to our control plane endpoints in the region you select \u0014 we can provide an isolation addendum for telemetry handling.

- Dedicated: we can provision capacity in eu-central-1 with explicit network routes to prevent egress. This is the recommended path if you need strict non-export of inference or cache state.

- Private (VPC): for absolute guarantees we recommend customer-managed VPC with a private control plane. In this model we avoid cross-border routing entirely; customer's network team must allow specific egress/peering rules we will provide.

I'll bring example network diagrams and a short checklist to the tech session. Recommended attendees from FinBank: Security Architecture + Network Engineering + Procurement.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
